prompts.text: Our group has to deliver a birthday cake like a secret mission. Who accidentally announces the plan on a loudspeaker?
Which friend could convincingly pretend to be an undercover detective for about thirty seconds?
A spy mission hidden inside a garden party or a mystery involving a missing library book?
Our secret headquarters would be discovered immediately because somebody insisted on installing a neon sign.
Tell me about a plan among friends that required far more secrecy than it actually deserved.
There's always one person who whispers more loudly than everybody else speaks.
What's the worst possible code name the group could give you?
We have to exchange a secret message using only fruit in a grocery basket. What's the system?
Disguises that are far too convincing or passwords nobody in the group can remember?
The most successful secret mission is the one where nobody gets distracted by snacks.
If our group traded skills for an afternoon, which friend's skill would you borrow first?
You have to teach someone a task in ten minutes while wearing oven mitts. What are you teaching?
Learning to decorate cakes from a friend or learning to take great portraits on a phone?
The person who says a skill is easy often forgets how long it took them to learn it.
Nobody should judge the first pancake made by someone who's teaching themselves to cook.
Tell me about a friend who patiently taught you something they genuinely could have done faster themselves.
Which unusual skill would earn the most tickets at our imaginary friendship skill fair?
Our group has to teach an alien three ordinary human activities. Which one gets the funniest explanation?
Learning a card trick from a friend or figuring out how to solve a Rubik's Cube together?
Being able to explain something simply is worth more than making the explanation sound impressive.
Our friend group adopts a pet tortoise. Who makes a detailed walking schedule for it?
What animal would best represent your friends' combined personality?
A very polite goat as our unofficial mascot or a sleepy owl that refuses to attend meetings?
An imaginary pet shared by several friends would have more nicknames than anyone could remember.
Everyone is brave about animal noises until the sound comes from inside an empty cupboard.
Tell me about an animal that made an unexpected guest appearance during a social gathering.
Which friend would be caught speaking to the group pet as though it understood complicated gossip?
Our mascot escapes with the list of birthday plans in its mouth. Who attempts negotiations?
Training a dog to fetch slippers or teaching a parrot a harmless catchphrase?
A dog with excellent manners would become the only reliable member of our planning committee.
What very ordinary thing in your neighbourhood deserves its own absurd tourist attraction?
We must persuade visitors that a tiny pothole is a historic monument. What's our official story?
A guided tour of unusual front doors or a museum dedicated entirely to everyday umbrellas?
Tell me about a tourist attraction you found much stranger than the promotional pictures suggested.
People queue for surprising things when there's a person nearby confidently describing them as famous.
Our imaginary tourist attraction would need a gift shop selling miniature replicas of a traffic cone.
Which friend would make the most convincing tour guide for an attraction that doesn't actually exist?
Someone asks why tourists are photographing an ordinary lamppost. How do we keep a straight face?
A guided walk with hilarious made-up facts or a treasure hunt with genuinely interesting local details?
What's the most unusual museum or small exhibition you've visited that turned out to be brilliant?
We're on a cooking show and the secret ingredient is popcorn. Which friend acts like this is a personal insult?
Who would introduce a plate of toast with a two-minute speech about artistic vision?
A cooking contest using five random ingredients or inventing desserts from things already in the fridge?
Somebody who can cook perfectly at home becomes strangely nervous when an audience watches.
Every kitchen has someone who tastes the sauce so often there won't be much left for dinner.
Tell me about a cooking mistake that became a surprisingly tasty result.
Which friend is most likely to measure every ingredient and then add 'a bit more' anyway?
We're given a whole watermelon and told to prepare a three-course meal. What is the first course?
Judging a pie contest or trying to invent the world's most unnecessary sandwich?
A cooking-show judge who laughs at their own descriptions would make every contestant feel better.
If your friendships gave you one harmless superpower, what would make everyday life more entertaining?
One friend can pause time for exactly eight seconds. What's the least useful way they could use it?
Being able to find any lost pen instantly or knowing exactly when an oven timer is about to ring?
The friend who always remembers birthdays might already have a superpower nobody appreciates.
Teleportation would ruin our group chat's tradition of debating travel times.
Tell me about a coincidence that felt like something from a superhero story.
Who would insist on designing costumes before we'd even discovered our powers?
Our friend group has to defeat a villain whose only weapon is making everyone sneeze. What's the plan?
The power to translate animal sounds or the ability to make broken zips work again?
The most useful superhero on a group holiday would be someone who could find free parking.
What ridiculous job title would you give a friend who's always organising people's birthdays?
We start a company where one employee is Chief Biscuit Officer. Who claims the role?
Director of Lost Socks or Executive Vice President of Finding Phone Chargers?
Some friends can turn choosing a restaurant into a full board meeting with minutes and action points.
Everybody should get one absurdly grand title for the practical thing they do best.
Tell me about a time you were given a responsibility you had absolutely not volunteered for.
Who would make the best head of a department dedicated to settling silly arguments?
Our imaginary boss demands a quarterly report on group laughter. What metric do we invent?
Manager of Dramatic Entrances or Head of Unexpected Snack Distribution?
Performance reviews among friends would end the moment anyone asked for examples.
If each friend had their own weather forecast, whose would involve a sudden unexpected thunderstorm?
A weather presenter hires our group to demonstrate four different kinds of wind. Who goes too far?
A surprise snowball fight on a sunny day or a beach picnic that needs enormous umbrellas?
People react to three drops of rain as if they've never encountered water from the sky before.
The friend who refuses to check the forecast should not be trusted with the outdoor event plan.
Tell me about a day whose weather transformed everyone's mood completely.
Who in your circle would willingly go outside just to feel an approaching storm?
We are told to pack for four seasons in one day, but we only have one suitcase. What's essential?
Watching distant lightning safely from indoors or running through light rain to reach a café?
The right rainy-day soundtrack can make a cancelled outing feel like a plan all along.
We invent a game where you must speak only in questions for five minutes. Who loses immediately?

prompts.text: What would the morning show on our friend group's radio station be called?
We're broadcasting live and a friend starts reading their grocery list as though it's breaking news. Who interrupts?
A late-night storytelling programme or an afternoon show dedicated to defending unpopular snacks?
The person with the most serious radio voice often has the least serious things to announce.
A good radio show is just a friendship group that happens to remember other people are listening.
Tell me about a funny announcement you heard that sounded too ridiculous to be real.
Which friend would host the call-in segment and forget to let the callers speak?
Our station must report on a neighbourhood cat's disappearance as a major developing story. What's the headline?
Taking turns choosing a mystery song or hosting a quiz where the answers are all terrible puns?
Our imaginary traffic report would somehow include updates about queues for the best roadside snacks.
